structure.overview: Edward Ryckman seeks judicial review of the Canada Revenue Agency's (CRA) decision denying his eligibility for the Canada Emergency Response Benefit (CERB) on the basis that he did not cease work due to COVID-19. The Federal Court found the CRA's decision unreasonable due to procedural unfairness, specifically the failure to consider key evidence submitted by Ryckman. The court set aside the decision and remitted the matter back to the CRA for redetermination, awarding Ryckman costs.

sections.label: Admissibility of evidence and procedural fairness issues
Reasoning on procedural fairness and reasons requirement

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Edward Ryckman seeks judicial review of CRA's decision denying CERB eligibility for not ceasing work due to COVID-19; court finds CRA's decision unreasonable.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: CRA informed Ryckman in Feb 2022 he was ineligible for CERB; after Second Review in Sept 2023, CRA confirmed ineligibility as work stoppage was pre-COVID.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: Ryckman sought judicial review of Second Review; Respondent agreed decision was unreasonable; Justice Heneghan set it aside and ordered redetermination.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: In July 2024, CRA Officer contacted Ryckman for info for Further Second Review; Ryckman submitted detailed evidence by Aug 8 deadline.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: Officer called Ryckman in Sept 2024 about return-to-work timeframe; Ryckman referred Officer to his affidavit as complete info.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: CRA decided again in Sept 2024 that Ryckman was ineligible for CERB as he did not stop work for COVID-19 reasons.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Court explains reasonableness review standard from Vavilov, emphasizing decision makers must address key issues to show sensitivity to the matter.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Respondent challenges admissibility of five exhibits not before Officer, including medical direction, prior judgment, and CERB Remission Order.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Court doubts Respondent's objections to some exhibits but finds no need to rule as they do not affect outcome.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Respondent relies on Officer's affidavit listing documents considered in Further Second Review, asserting list is complete.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Court finds Officer did not consider Ryckman's July 2024 Application Record despite receiving it; Respondent concedes this at hearing.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Officer's failure to consider central evidence is reviewable error causing procedural unfairness and unreasonable decision, per case law.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Having found unreasonableness, court declines to address other Ryckman arguments.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Court orders matter remitted to CRA for redetermination, deferring to CRA's expertise on eligibility assessment.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Ryckman requests order compelling CRA to provide reasons if ineligible again; court finds no need as CRA must comply with binding jurisprudence.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Court awards Ryckman $1,500 costs despite Respondent's objection, citing discretion and promoting settlement in future cases.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Court states decision makers must provide reasons addressing central issues to show they listened, rooted in procedural fairness and right to be heard.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Court explains decision makers need not address every argument but must grapple with key issues to show alertness; failure may undermine decision validity.
